air-race-pylon.context: A tall tapered pylon gate on a base with a small airplane banking past it. Used for air racing, air show and aerobatic event content.

seatback-pocket.context: The back of an airline seat with a pocket holding a safety card and a magazine. Used for in-flight amenities, cabin information and seat features.

cabin-interphone.context: A wall handset on a coiled cord beside a keypad panel. Used for crew call systems and communication between flight attendants and the cockpit.

engine-indicating-display.context: A cockpit screen with two round arc gauges and bar graphs beneath them. Used for engine monitoring, avionics and flight deck instrument content.

airworthiness-certificate.context: A framed certificate showing a small airplane above a round seal. Used for aircraft registration, inspection approval and compliance records.

drop-zone-target.context: A parachute canopy descending toward a round bullseye target on the ground. Used for skydiving landing areas, accuracy landing and airdrop content.

crew-rest-bunk.context: A small enclosed bunk with a pillow and a curtain partly drawn across it. Used for crew rest areas on long haul flights and sleeping berths.

anti-collision-beacon.context: A side view of an airplane fuselage with a small dome lamp on top giving off flashing rays. Used for aircraft lighting and ground safety content.

gate-check-tag.context: A luggage tag on a looped strap printed with a stroller symbol. Used for gate checked strollers and child equipment handled at the boarding gate.

wing-spoiler.context: A wing cross section with a panel raised from its upper surface and airflow lines breaking behind it. Used for flight control, airbrake and aerodynamics content.

helicopter-collective.context: An angled lever rising from a cockpit floor with a twist grip on its end beside the edge of a pilot seat. Used for helicopter controls and rotorcraft flight training.

hand-propping.context: A person standing in front of a small plane nose, reaching up to swing the propeller down by hand. Used for starting vintage and light aircraft engines.
